title: Heat pump or furnace plus air conditioning? One study's medians were $270 apart.

sentences.text: Heat pump, or furnace plus air conditioning? One study's median installed costs came out $270 apart.

assertions.text: In the study's median installation costs, a heat pump ($6,185) came out $270 below the median of the most expensive system, a natural gas furnace plus AC.
qualifications: s02 says the figures are one study's national medians rather than contractor quotes; s03 says more than 80 percent of the other systems' cost distributions overlap the heat pump's; s04 gives the Canadian model that disagrees on upfront cost; s05 says the comparison counts cooling on both sides.

sentences.note: Copied from parent s10.a. The eyebrow is ONE FIGURE FROM THE RECORD, so the opening is the $270 itself.

sentences.text: Those are one study's national medians, not quotes for your house: the heat pump's median landed just under the gas furnace with air conditioning.

assertions.text: The study's figures are medians of installation cost rather than contractor quotes: the heat pump's median ($6,185) is $270 below the median of the most expensive system, a natural gas furnace plus AC.
qualifications: s02 itself says the figures are one study's medians rather than quotes for the viewer's own house; s03 gives the overlap in the cost distributions behind them; s04 gives the model that disagrees.

sentences.note: Revision 3, answering the blocking finding on revision 2: the $6,185 median is priced in 2020 dollars at one assumed capacity (the study's methods line, edwards-2024 L1810-L1817), and this Short cannot date it out loud: that methods line is not a cited passage of this claim, a Short never adds a verdict or a passage, and any spoken year would be a figure with no cited passage behind it. So the absolute price is no longer spoken at all. The Short keeps what the dollar year does not touch, as the finding said: the $270 gap in s01 and the overlap in s03, both measured in the same dollars on both sides. The sentence still carries the qualification the Short must carry here, that these are one study's national medians and not quotes for the viewer's house.

sentences.text: More than 80 percent of the other systems' cost distributions overlap the heat pump's.

assertions.text: More than 80% of the installation cost distributions for the other systems overlap with the cost distribution for a heat pump.
qualifications: s03 is itself the qualification on the gap in s01: the systems' price ranges overlap by more than 80 percent, so the medians sit close together inside a wide spread; s04 gives the model that disagrees with the parity reading altogether.

sentences.text: A Canadian model disagrees, putting heat pumps higher upfront than gas heating with air conditioning, ahead only over the system's life.

assertions.text: The Canadian model finds heat pumps have higher upfront costs than gas-fired heating with air conditioning, and are cost-competitive over the life of the system through their efficiency and doubling as cooling.
qualifications: s04 is itself the disagreement the record holds against s01 and s02: it is one model's upfront finding, against the installed medians the study measured, and the sentence says in place that the model's advantage arrives only over the system's life.

sentences.note: Copied from parent s12.a, narrowed to what this Short's claim needs: the upfront direction and the lifetime reversal, without the model's wider lowest-cost conclusion.

sentences.text: Cooling is counted on both sides here: take the air conditioner out of your quote, and the heat pump is the bigger number.

assertions.text: The $270 gap is measured against a natural gas furnace plus AC, so it counts cooling on both sides and is not a comparison with replacing a furnace on its own, which buys no cooling.
qualifications: s05 itself limits the finding to a baseline that includes cooling: against a furnace on its own the heat pump is the bigger number.

sentences.note: The parent's furnace-alone figures (s07, s08) rest on heat-pumps/heat-pump-costs-more-buy-install, a claim outside this Short's package, so the direction is said without a figure: the cited baseline buys an air conditioner, and a furnace-only baseline does not.

sentences.text: Which comparison fits your house is the question the full inquiry takes on.
